1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 PWC worker and CPU1 ready handshake.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: #include <stdint.h>
7: #include <stdbool.h>
8: #include <stdio.h>
9: 
10: #include <nuttx/semaphore.h>
11: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
12: #include <nuttx/signal.h>
13: #include <nuttx/kthread.h>
14: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
15: 
16: #include "bk7258_psram.h"
17: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
18: 
19: #define PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD 0x5u
20: #define PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD 0x7u
21: #define PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD 0x8u
22: #define PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD 0x9u
23: #define PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD 0xau
24: #define PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1 11u
25: #define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON 0u
26: #define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF 1u
27: #define PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT 0u
28: #define PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH 1u
29: #define PM_QUEUE_DEPTH 8u
30: #define PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS 500u
31: #define PM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS 1000u
32: 
33: struct pwc_message
34: {
35:   uint32_t header;
36:   uint32_t param1;
37:   uint32_t param2;
38:   uint32_t param3;
39: };
40: 
41: static struct pwc_message g_queue[PM_QUEUE_DEPTH];
42: static volatile unsigned int g_head;
43: static volatile unsigned int g_tail;
44: static sem_t g_pwc_sem;
45: static sem_t g_worker_sem;
46: static sem_t g_psram_power_sem;
47: static volatile bool g_worker_ready;
48: static volatile bool g_ready_sent;
49: static volatile bool g_psram_power_waiting;
50: static volatile uint32_t g_psram_power_state;
51: 
52: static void psram_power_vote_rollback(void)
53: {
54:   int ret;
55: 
56:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,
57:                                 PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
58:                                 PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF, 0);
59:   if (ret >= 0)
60:     {
61:       ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
62:     }
63: 
64:   if (ret < 0)
65:     {
66:       printf("PWC: PSRAM power vote rollback failed, error=%d\n", ret);
67:     }
68: }
69: 
70: static int ipc_heartbeat_worker(int argc, char **argv)
71: {
72:   static uint32_t heartbeat_payload;
73: 
74:   (void)argc;
75:   (void)argv;
76:   for (;;)
77:     {
78:       nxsig_usleep(2000000);
79:       (void)bk7258_mbox_send_message(2, 0x10,
80:                                      (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&heartbeat_payload,
81:                                      sizeof(heartbeat_payload), 0);
82:     }
83:   return 0;
84: }
85: 
86: static void pwc_rx(const void *raw)
87: {
88:   const uint8_t *bytes = raw;
89:   struct pwc_message message;
90:   unsigned int next = (g_head + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
91:   if (next == g_tail || bytes == NULL)
92:     {
93:       return;
94:     }
95:   message.header = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[0];
96:   message.param1 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[1];
97:   message.param2 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[2];
98:   message.param3 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[3];
99:   g_queue[g_head] = message;
100:   g_head = next;
101:   nxsem_post(&g_pwc_sem);
102: }
103: 
104: static int pwc_worker(int argc, char **argv)
105: {
106:   (void)argc;
107:   (void)argv;
108:   g_worker_ready = true;
109:   nxsem_post(&g_worker_sem);
110:   for (;;)
111:     {
112:       struct pwc_message message;
113:       nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&g_pwc_sem);
114:       message = g_queue[g_tail];
115:       g_tail = (g_tail + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
116:       /* Hardware power/clock actions stay in this thread, never in IRQ. */
117:       switch (message.header & 0xffu)
118:         {
119:           case PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD:
120:             /* The unmodified AVDK SMP firmware returns the requested ON/OFF
121:              * state in param1. It does not expose the PSRAM driver result or
122:              * detected capacity, so AP validates its configured regions with
123:              * the non-destructive boundary probe before creating allocators.
124:              */
125: 
126:             g_psram_power_state = message.param1;
127:             if (g_psram_power_waiting)
128:               {
129:                 g_psram_power_waiting = false;
130:                 nxsem_post(&g_psram_power_sem);
131:               }
132:             break;
133: 
134: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
135:           case PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD:
136:             if (message.param1 == 0u)
137:               {
138:                 (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
139:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
140:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
141:                   bk7258_psram_heap_used(), 0);
142:               }
143:             else if (message.param1 == PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF)
144:               {
145:                 /* This CP notification is sent after physical power-down. */
146: 
147:                 bk7258_psram_power_lost();
148:               }
149:             break;
150: 
151:           case PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD:
152:             bk7258_psram_dump();
153:             break;
154: 
155:           case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
156:             {
157:               int ret = bk7258_psram_shutdown();
158: 
159:               (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
160:                 PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD, PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
161:                 ret == 0 ? PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH :
162:                            PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT, 0);
163:             }
164:             break;
165: #endif
166: 
167:           default:
168:             break;
169:         }
170:     }
171:   return 0;
172: }
173: 
174: int bk7258_pwc_start(void)
175: {
176:   int pid;
177:   int ret;
178: 
179:   nxsem_init(&g_pwc_sem, 0, 0);
180:   nxsem_init(&g_worker_sem, 0, 0);
181:   nxsem_init(&g_psram_power_sem, 0, 0);
182:   g_head = 0;
183:   g_tail = 0;
184:   g_worker_ready = false;
185:   g_ready_sent = false;
186:   g_psram_power_waiting = false;
187:   g_psram_power_state = PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF;
188:   bk7258_mailbox_set_pwc_rx(pwc_rx);
189:   /* Match Armino mb_ipc_heartbeat: notify CPU0 before PM ready and keep the
190:    * CPU1 liveness indication independent from the PWC worker. */
191:   if (bk7258_mbox_send_message(1, 0x10, 0, 0, 0) != 0)
192:     {
193:       return -1;
194:     }
195: 
196:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_hw_control(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
197:   if (ret < 0)
198:     {
199:       printf("PWC: IPC power-up transport timeout, error=%d\n", ret);
200:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
201:       return ret;
202:     }
203:   printf("PWC: IPC power-up transport complete\n");
204: 
205:   if (kthread_create("ipc-heartbeat", 100, 1536, ipc_heartbeat_worker,
206:                      NULL) < 0)
207:     {
208:       return -1;
209:     }
210:   pid = kthread_create("pwc", 110, 2048, pwc_worker, NULL);
211:   if (pid < 0)
212:     {
213:       return pid;
214:     }
215:   if (nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_worker_sem, MSEC2TICK(200)) < 0 ||
216:       !g_worker_ready)
217:     {
218:       printf("PWC: worker start timeout\n");
219:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
220:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
221:     }
222:   printf("PWC: worker ready\n");
223: 
224:   /* CP boots CPU1 from its low-power worker and waits there for this ready
225:    * command. Send it before requesting PSRAM, whose vote is handled by that
226:    * same worker, otherwise the two cores deadlock waiting for each other.
227:    */
228: 
229:   g_ready_sent = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD,
230:                                          1, 0, 0) == 0;
231:   if (!g_ready_sent)
232:     {
233:       printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready queue failed\n");
234:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
235:       return -EIO;
236:     }
237: 
238:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
239:   if (ret < 0)
240:     {
241:       printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready transport timeout, error=%d\n", ret);
242:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
243:       return ret;
244:     }
245: 
246:   printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready acknowledged by CP transport\n");
247: 
248: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
249:   g_psram_power_waiting = true;
250:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,
251:                                 PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
252:                                 PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON, 0);
253:   if (ret >= 0)
254:     {
255:       ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_psram_power_sem,
256:                          MSEC2TICK(PM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS));
257:     }
258: 
259:   g_psram_power_waiting = false;
260:   if (ret < 0 || g_psram_power_state != PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON)
261:     {
262:       printf("PWC: PSRAM power response failed, error=%d state=%lu\n",
263:              ret, (unsigned long)g_psram_power_state);
264:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
265:       psram_power_vote_rollback();
266: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM_REQUIRED
267:       return ret < 0 ? ret : -EIO;
268: #endif
269:     }
270:   else
271:     {
272:       /* printf("PWC: PSRAM power vote ON acknowledged\n"); */
273:       ret = bk7258_psram_initialize();
274:       if (ret < 0)
275:         {
276:           printf("PWC: PSRAM allocator initialization failed, error=%d\n",
277:                  ret);
278:           psram_power_vote_rollback();
279: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM_REQUIRED
280:           return ret;
281: #endif
282:         }
283:       else
284:         {
285:           /* printf("PWC: PSRAM allocators ONLINE\n"); */
286:         }
287:     }
288: #endif
289: 
290:   if (g_ready_sent)
291:     {
292:       return 0;
293:     }
294: 
295:   return -1;
296: }

431: {

461: 	clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
462: 	if(((clk_param >> 0x4)&0x3) > cksel_core)//when it from the higher frequency to lower frequency
463: 	{
464: 		/*1.core clk select*/
465: 		clk_param = 0;
466: 		clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
467: 		clk_param &=  ~(0x3 << 4);
468: 		clk_param |=  cksel_core << 4;
469: 		sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_set(CLK_DIV_REG0,clk_param);
470: 
471: 		/*2.config bus and core clk div*/
472: 		clk_param = 0;
473: 		clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
474: 		clk_param &=  ~(0xF << 0);
475: 		clk_param |=  ckdiv_core << 0;
476: 		sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_set(CLK_DIV_REG0,clk_param);
477: 
478: 		/*3.config cpu clk div*/
479: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(0,ckdiv_cpu0);
480: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(1,ckdiv_cpu1);
481: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(2,1);//config cpu2
482: 	}
483: 	else//when it from the lower frequency to higher frequency
484: 	{
485: 		/*1.config bus and core clk div*/
486: 		if(ckdiv_core == 0)
487: 		{
488: 			sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(0,ckdiv_cpu0);//avoid the bus freq > 240m
489: 		}
490: 
491: 		clk_param = 0;
492: 		clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
493: 		clk_param &=  ~(0xF << 0);
494: 		clk_param |=  ckdiv_core << 0;
495: 		sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_set(CLK_DIV_REG0,clk_param);
496: 
497: 		/*2.config cpu clk div*/
498: 		if(ckdiv_core != 0)
499: 		{
500: 			sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(0,ckdiv_cpu0);
501: 		}
502: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(1,ckdiv_cpu1);
503: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(2,1);//config cpu2
504: 
505: 		/*3.core clk select*/
506: 
507: 		clk_param = 0;
508: 		clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
509: 		clk_param &=  ~(0x3 << 4);
510: 		clk_param |=  cksel_core << 4;
511: 		sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_set(CLK_DIV_REG0,clk_param);
512: 	}
513: 
514: 	return BK_OK;

1: 如何动态切换CPU主频
2: ==================================================
3: 
4: 切换时钟的策略
5: -----------------------------------------------------
6: - 1.配置CPU主频统一在CPU0上(避免多核操作相同的寄存器不同步而出现异常)。
7: - 2.CPU选择投频最高的模块的CPU主频。
8: - 3.支持CPU0和CPU1调用bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq()接口投频，不支持CPU2上调用该接口。
9: - 4.启动CPU1时，当前SDK默认把主频升到最高，应用程序可以不用额外再调接口投频。
10: - 5.CPU0或CPU1上调接口投频之后，CPU0,CPU1,CPU2的主频和BUS频率都会变化。因为他们的频率是联动的，不是独立的。
11: 
12: 
13: 支持配置的CPU主频
14: -----------------------------------------------------
15: 投频后CPU和BUS的频率对应关系：
16:     - 0. PM_CPU_FRQ_26M = 0,  // 0:CPU1:26M,CPU0:26M,BUS:26M
17:     - 1. PM_CPU_FRQ_60M,      // 1:CPU1:60M,CPU0:60M,BUS:60M
18:     - 2. PM_CPU_FRQ_80M,      // 2:CPU1:80M,CPU0:80M,BUS:80M
19:     - 3. PM_CPU_FRQ_120M,     // 3:CPU1:120M,CPU0:120M,BUS:120M
20:     - 4. PM_CPU_FRQ_240M,     // 4:CPU1:240M,CPU0:120m,BUS:120M
21:     - 5. PM_CPU_FRQ_320M,     // 5:CPU1:320M,CPU0:160M,BUS:160M
22:     - 6. PM_CPU_FRQ_480M,     // 6:CPU1:480M,CPU0:240M,BUS:240M
23:     - 7. PM_CPU_FRQ_DEFAULT   // default cpu frequency which control by pm module
24: 
25: 
26: 动态投CPU主频的接口
27: -----------------------------------------------------
28:  - bk_err_t bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq(pm_dev_id_e module,pm_cpu_freq_e cpu_freq);
29:     - module：模块名字（选择一个使用的模块，如果自己新的模块，可以添加）
30:     - cpu_freq：需要投的主频
31: 
32: 
33: 获取当前投的最高CPU主频的接口
34: -----------------------------------------------------
35: pm_cpu_freq_e bk_pm_current_max_cpu_freq_get()
36: 
37: 示例：参考以下步骤1和步骤2
38: -----------------------------------------------------
39:  - 步骤1： DISP模块投320M:
40:    - bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq(PM_DEV_ID_DISP, PM_CPU_FRQ_320M);
41: 
42:  - 步骤2： DISP模块使用完高平后，把自己的模块主频恢复默认：
43:    - bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq(PM_DEV_ID_DISP, PM_CPU_FRQ_DEFAULT);
44: 
45: 
46: .. note::
47:    投频使用的dev_id和使用完之后的dev_id需要一样，不然会引起错误。使用前可以搜索,确认DEV_ID是其他模块没有其他业务使用

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 MBOX0 v2 physical transport.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <errno.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <string.h>
11: 
12: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
13: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
14: 
15: #include "arm_internal.h"
16: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
17: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
18: #include "irq.h"
19: 
20: #define MBOX_REG(n)             (BK7258_MBOX0_BASE + ((n) * 4u))
21: #define MBOX_CH1_CFG            MBOX_REG(0x20)
22: #define MBOX_CH1_FIFO_CFG       MBOX_REG(0x21)
23: #define MBOX_CH1_TDATA0         MBOX_REG(0x22)
24: #define MBOX_CH1_TDATA1         MBOX_REG(0x23)
25: #define MBOX_CH1_TID            MBOX_REG(0x24)
26: #define MBOX_CH1_SID            MBOX_REG(0x25)
27: #define MBOX_CH1_RDATA0         MBOX_REG(0x26)
28: #define MBOX_CH1_RDATA1         MBOX_REG(0x27)
29: #define MBOX_CH1_STATUS         MBOX_REG(0x28)
30: #define MBOX_CH0_STATUS         MBOX_REG(0x18)
31: #define MBOX_CH2_STATUS         MBOX_REG(0x38)
32: #define MBOX_CTRL               MBOX_REG(2)
33: 
34: #define MBOX_CFG_INT_EN         (1u << 8)
35: #define MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN       (1u << 9)
36: #define MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN       (1u << 10)
37: #define MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN      (1u << 11)
38: #define MBOX_CFG_WRERR_STATUS   (1u << 16)
39: #define MBOX_CFG_RDERR_STATUS   (1u << 17)
40: #define MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_STATUS  (1u << 18)
41: #define MBOX_CFG_ERROR_STATUS   (MBOX_CFG_WRERR_STATUS | \
42:                                  MBOX_CFG_RDERR_STATUS | \
43:                                  MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_STATUS)
44: #define MBOX_CFG_RW_MASK        0x00000fffu
45: 
46: #define MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT      (2u * 3u + 1u)
47: 
48: struct mbox_rx_descriptor
49: {
50:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
51:   uint32_t order;
52:   bool used;
53: };
54: 
55: static bk7258_mbox_callback_t g_callback;
56: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor g_rx_desc[MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT];
57: static uint32_t g_rx_order;
58: static uint32_t g_processing_order;
59: static bool g_mbox_ready;
60: static struct bk7258_mbox_stats g_stats;
61: 
62: _Static_assert(MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT > 2u * 3u,
63:                "RX descriptors must hold a deferred command and two FIFOs");
64: 
65: uint32_t bk7258_mbox_rx_status(void)
66: {
67:   return getreg32(MBOX_CH1_STATUS);
68: }
69: 
70: static void mbox_clear_errors(void)
71: {
72:   uint32_t config = getreg32(MBOX_CH1_CFG);
73:   uint32_t errors = config & MBOX_CFG_ERROR_STATUS;
74: 
75:   if ((errors & MBOX_CFG_WRERR_STATUS) != 0)
76:     {
77:       g_stats.write_error++;
78:     }
79: 
80:   if ((errors & MBOX_CFG_RDERR_STATUS) != 0)
81:     {
82:       g_stats.read_error++;
83:     }
84: 
85:   if ((errors & MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_STATUS) != 0)
86:     {
87:       g_stats.write_full++;
88:     }
89: 
90:   if (errors != 0)
91:     {
92:       putreg32((config & MBOX_CFG_RW_MASK) | errors, MBOX_CH1_CFG);
93:     }
94: }
95: 
96: static bool mbox_valid_envelope(uint8_t source, uint32_t address,
97:                                 uint32_t length)
98: {
99:   if (source != 0)
100:     {
101:       g_stats.bad_source++;
102:       return false;
103:     }
104: 
105:   if (length != BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
106:     {
107:       g_stats.bad_length++;
108:       return false;
109:     }
110: 
111:   if ((address & 3u) != 0 || address < BK7258_CP_RAM_START ||
112:       address > BK7258_CP_RAM_END - BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
113:     {
114:       g_stats.bad_address++;
115:       return false;
116:     }
117: 
118:   return true;
119: }
120: 
121: int bk7258_mbox_send(uint8_t destination, const uint32_t data[2])
122: {
123:   uintptr_t status;
124: 
125:   if (!g_mbox_ready || destination > 2 || data == NULL)
126:     {
127:       return -EINVAL;
128:     }
129: 
130:   /* CPU1 transmits through channel 1.  Full is reported by the target's
131:    * receive FIFO status register.
132:    */
133: 
134:   status = destination == 0 ? MBOX_CH0_STATUS :
135:            destination == 1 ? MBOX_CH1_STATUS : MBOX_CH2_STATUS;
136:   if ((getreg32(status) & 1u) != 0)
137:     {
138:       return -EAGAIN;
139:     }
140: 
141:   putreg32(data[0], MBOX_CH1_TDATA0);
142:   putreg32(data[1], MBOX_CH1_TDATA1);
143:   putreg32(destination, MBOX_CH1_TID);
144:   return OK;
145: }
146: 
147: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_alloc_desc(void)
148: {
149:   unsigned int i;
150: 
151:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
152:     {
153:       if (!g_rx_desc[i].used)
154:         {
155:           return &g_rx_desc[i];
156:         }
157:     }
158: 
159:   return NULL;
160: }
161: 
162: static bool mbox_priority_message(
163:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
164: {
165:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
166: 
167:   return (control & (BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0;
168: }
169: 
170: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_oldest_desc(bool priority)
171: {
172:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *oldest = NULL;
173:   unsigned int i;
174: 
175:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
176:     {
177:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc = &g_rx_desc[i];
178: 
179:       if (!desc->used || mbox_priority_message(&desc->message) != priority)
180:         {
181:           continue;
182:         }
183: 
184:       if (oldest == NULL || (int32_t)(desc->order - oldest->order) < 0)
185:         {
186:           oldest = desc;
187:         }
188:     }
189: 
190:   return oldest;
191: }
192: 
193: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
194: {
195:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
196:   int ret;
197: 
198:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
199:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
200:    */
201: 
202:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
203:     {
204:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
205:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
206:       g_processing_order = 0;
207:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
208:         {
209:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
210:           break;
211:         }
212: 
213:       desc->used = false;
214:     }
215: 
216:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
217:     {
218:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
219:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
220:       g_processing_order = 0;
221:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
222:         {
223:           break;
224:         }
225: 
226:       desc->used = false;
227:     }
228: }
229: 
230: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
231: {
232:   (void)irq;
233:   (void)context;
234:   (void)arg;
235: 
236:   mbox_clear_errors();
237: 
238:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0)
239:     {
240:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
241:       uint32_t address;
242:       uint32_t length;
243:       uint8_t source;
244: 
245:       mbox_process_desc();
246:       desc = mbox_alloc_desc();
247:       if (desc == NULL)
248:         {
249:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
250:           break;
251:         }
252: 
253:       source = getreg32(MBOX_CH1_SID) & 0x0fu;
254:       address = getreg32(MBOX_CH1_RDATA0);
255:       length = getreg32(MBOX_CH1_RDATA1);
256:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
257:         {
258:           continue;
259:         }
260: 
261:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
262:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
263:              sizeof(desc->message));
264:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
265:       desc->used = true;
266:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
267:       mbox_process_desc();
268:     }
269: 
270:   mbox_process_desc();
271: 
272:   return OK;
273: }
274: 
275: void bk7258_mbox_set_callback(bk7258_mbox_callback_t callback)
276: {
277:   g_callback = callback;
278: }
279: 
280: void bk7258_mbox_kick_rx(void)
281: {
282:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
283: 
284:   (void)bk7258_mbox_irq(0, NULL, NULL);
285:   up_irq_restore(flags);
286: }
287: 
288: void bk7258_mbox_discard_deferred(void)
289: {
290:   unsigned int i;
291: 
292:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
293:     {
294:       if (g_rx_desc[i].used && g_processing_order != 0 &&
295:           (int32_t)(g_rx_desc[i].order - g_processing_order) < 0 &&
296:           !mbox_priority_message(&g_rx_desc[i].message))
297:         {
298:           g_rx_desc[i].used = false;
299:         }
300:     }
301: }
302: 
303: void bk7258_mbox_get_stats(struct bk7258_mbox_stats *stats)
304: {
305:   irqstate_t flags;
306: 
307:   if (stats == NULL)
308:     {
309:       return;
310:     }
311: 
312:   flags = up_irq_save();
313:   *stats = g_stats;
314:   up_irq_restore(flags);
315: }
316: 
317: int bk7258_mbox_init(void)
318: {
319:   int ret;
320: 
321:   if (g_mbox_ready)
322:     {
323:       return OK;
324:     }
325: 
326:   memset(g_rx_desc, 0, sizeof(g_rx_desc));
327:   g_rx_order = 0;
328:   g_processing_order = 0;
329:   memset(&g_stats, 0, sizeof(g_stats));
330: 
331:   /* CPU1 owns channel 1 and FIFO entries 2..4.  Install the callback and
332:    * descriptors before enabling the route; pre-existing FIFO entries are
333:    * then processed normally instead of being blindly discarded.
334:    */
335: 
336:   putreg32(2u | MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
337:            MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN, MBOX_CH1_CFG);
338:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), MBOX_CH1_FIFO_CFG);
339:   modifyreg32(MBOX_CTRL, 0, 1u << 2);
340:   mbox_clear_errors();
341: 
342:   ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX, bk7258_mbox_irq, NULL);
343:   if (ret < 0)
344:     {
345:       return ret;
346:     }
347: 
348:   g_mbox_ready = true;
349:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1, 0, 1u << 31);
350:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX);
351:   return OK;
352: }

81:  ****************************************************************************/

83: static void fifo_drain(void)
84: {
85:   putreg32(0, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST);
86: 
87:   while (getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD)

90:     }

97:  *
98:  * Description:
99:  *   Communicate with CPU Core 1 using inter-processor FIFO for boot
100:  *

102:  *   msg - Data to be sent to Core 1
103:  *
104:  * Returned Value:
105:  *   true on success; false on failure.
106:  *
107:  ****************************************************************************/

109: static int fifo_comm(uint32_t msg)
110: {
111:   uint32_t rcv;
112: 
113:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_RDY))
114:     ;
115:   putreg32(msg, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_WR);
116:   __asm__ volatile ("sev");
117: 
118:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD))
119:     __asm__ volatile ("wfe");
120: 
121:   rcv = getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_RD);
122: 
123:   return msg == rcv;

174: /****************************************************************************
175:  * Name: up_cpu_start
176:  *
177:  * Description:
178:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
179:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
180:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
181:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
182:  *
183:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
184:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
185:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
186:  *   initialized.
187:  *
188:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
189:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
190:  *
191:  * Input Parameters:
192:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
193:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
194:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
195:  *
196:  * Returned Value:
197:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/
200: 
201: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
202: {
203:   int i;
204:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
205:   uint32_t core1_boot_msg[5];
206: 
207:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
208: 
209: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
210:   /* Notify of the start event */
211: 
212:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
213: #endif
214: 
215:   /* Reset Core 1 */
216: 
217:   setbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
218:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF) & RP2040_PSM_PROC1))
219:     ;
220:   clrbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
221: 
222:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
223: 
224:   /* Send initial VTOR, MSP, PC for Core 1 boot */
225: 
226:   core1_boot_msg[0] = 0;
227:   core1_boot_msg[1] = 1;
228:   core1_boot_msg[2] = getreg32(ARMV6M_SYSCON_VECTAB);
229:   core1_boot_msg[3] = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
230:                                 tcb->adj_stack_size;
231:   core1_boot_msg[4] = (uint32_t)core1_boot;
232: 
233:   do
234:     {
235:       fifo_drain();
236:       for (i = 0; i < 5; i++)
237:         {
238:           if (!fifo_comm(core1_boot_msg[i]))
239:             {
240:               break;
241:             }
242:         }
243:     }
244:   while (i < 5);
245: 
246:   fifo_drain();
247: 
248:   /* Enable inter-processor FIFO interrupt */
249: 
250:   irq_attach(RP2040_SMP_CALL_PROC0, rp2040_smp_call_handler, NULL);
251:   up_enable_irq(RP2040_SMP_CALL_PROC0);
252: 
253:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
254: 
255:   /* CPU Core 1 boot done */
256: 
257:   spin_unlock(&g_core1_boot);
258: 
259:   return 0;
260: }
261: 
262: #endif /* CONFIG_SMP */

41:  * Name: up_cpu_idlestack
42:  *
43:  * Description:
44:  *   Allocate a stack for the CPU[n] IDLE task (n > 0) if appropriate and
45:  *   setup up stack-related information in the IDLE task's TCB.  This
46:  *   function is always called before up_cpu_start().  This function is
47:  *   only called for the CPU's initial IDLE task; up_create_task is used for
48:  *   all normal tasks, pthreads, and kernel threads for all CPUs.
49:  *
50:  *   The initial IDLE task is a special case because the CPUs can be started
51:  *   in different wans in different environments:
52:  *
53:  *   1. The CPU may already have been started and waiting in a low power
54:  *      state for up_cpu_start().  In this case, the IDLE thread's stack
55:  *      has already been allocated and is already in use.  Here
56:  *      up_cpu_idlestack() only has to provide information about the
57:  *      already allocated stack.
58:  *
59:  *   2. The CPU may be disabled but started when up_cpu_start() is called.
60:  *      In this case, a new stack will need to be created for the IDLE
61:  *      thread and this function is then equivalent to:
62:  *
63:  *      return up_create_stack(tcb, stack_size, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL);
64:  *
65:  *   The following TCB fields must be initialized by this function:
66:  *
67:  *   - adj_stack_size: Stack size after adjustment for hardware, processor,
68:  *     etc.  This value is retained only for debug purposes.
69:  *   - stack_alloc_ptr: Pointer to allocated stack
70:  *   - stack_base_ptr: Adjusted stack base pointer after the TLS Data and
71:  *     Arguments has been removed from the stack allocation.
72:  *
73:  * Input Parameters:
74:  *   - cpu:         CPU index that indicates which CPU the IDLE task is
75:  *                  being created for.
76:  *   - tcb:         The TCB of new CPU IDLE task
77:  *   - stack_size:  The requested stack size for the IDLE task.  At least
78:  *                  this much must be allocated.  This should be
79:  *                  CONFIG_SMP_STACK_SIZE.
80:  *
81:  ****************************************************************************/
82: 
83: int up_cpu_idlestack(int cpu, struct tcb_s *tcb, size_t stack_size)
84: {
85: #if CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS > 1
86:   up_create_stack(tcb, stack_size, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL);
87: #endif
88:   return OK;
89: }

91: int rp2040_smp_call_handler(int irq, void *c, void *arg)
92: {
93:   int cpu = this_cpu();
94:   int irqreq;
95:   uint32_t stat;
96: 
97:   nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, c, arg);
98: 
99:   stat = getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST);
100:   if (stat & (RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_ROE | RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_WOF))
101:     {
102:       /* Clear sticky flag */
103: 
104:       putreg32(0, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST);
105:     }
106: 
107:   if (!(stat & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD))
108:     {
109:       /* No data received */
110: 
111:       return OK;
112:     }
113: 
114:   irqreq = getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_RD);
115: 
116:   if (irqreq != 0)
117:     {
118:       /* Handle IRQ enable/disable request */
119: 
120:       rp2040_handle_irqreq(irqreq);
121:       return OK;
122:     }
123: 
124:   DPRINTF("cpu%d will be paused\n", cpu);
125: 
126:   nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
127: 
128:   return OK;
129: }

155:     ;

42: /****************************************************************************
43:  * Name: up_initial_state
44:  *
45:  * Description:
46:  *   A new thread is being started and a new TCB
47:  *   has been created. This function is called to initialize
48:  *   the processor specific portions of the new TCB.
49:  *
50:  *   This function must setup the initial architecture registers
51:  *   and/or  stack so that execution will begin at tcb->start
52:  *   on the next context switch.
53:  *
54:  ****************************************************************************/
55: 
56: void up_initial_state(struct tcb_s *tcb)
57: {
58:   struct xcptcontext *xcp = &tcb->xcp;
59: 
60:   /* Initialize the initial exception register context structure */
61: 
62:   memset(xcp, 0, sizeof(struct xcptcontext));
63: 
64:   /* Initialize the idle thread stack */
65: 
66:   if (tcb->pid == IDLE_PROCESS_ID)
67:     {
68:       tcb->stack_alloc_ptr = (void *)(g_idle_topstack -
69:                                       CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE);
70:       tcb->stack_base_ptr  = tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
71:       tcb->adj_stack_size  = CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE;
72: 
73: #ifdef CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION
74:       /* If stack debug is enabled, then fill the stack with a
75:        * recognizable value that we can use later to test for high
76:        * water marks.
77:        */
78: 
79:       arm_stack_color(tcb->stack_alloc_ptr, 0);
80: #endif /* CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION */
81: 
82:       return;
83:     }
84: 
85:   /* Initialize the context registers to stack top */
86: 
87:   xcp->regs = (void *)((uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
88:                                  tcb->adj_stack_size -
89:                                  XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE);
90: 
91:   /* Initialize the xcp registers */
92: 
93:   memset(xcp->regs, 0, XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE);
94: 
95:   /* Save the initial stack pointer */
96: 
97:   xcp->regs[REG_SP]      = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
98:                                      tcb->adj_stack_size;
99: 
100: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK
101:   /* Set the stack limit value */
102: 
103:   xcp->regs[REG_R10]     = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_alloc_ptr + 64;
104: #endif
105: 
106: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
107:   /* Save the stack limit value, will be used in context switch. */
108: 
109:   xcp->regs[REG_SPLIM]   = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
110: #endif
111: 
112:   /* Save the task entry point (stripping off the thumb bit) */
113: 
114:   xcp->regs[REG_PC]      = (uint32_t)tcb->start & ~1;
115: 
116:   /* Specify thumb mode */
117: 
118:   xcp->regs[REG_XPSR]    = ARM_XPSR_T;
119: 
120:   /* All tasks need to set pic address to special register */
121: 
122: #ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_PIC
123:   __asm__ ("mov %0, r9" : "=r"(xcp->regs[REG_R9]));
124: #endif
125: 
126:   /* If this task is running PIC, then set the PIC base register to the
127:    * address of the allocated D-Space region.
128:    */
129: 
130: #ifdef CONFIG_PIC
131:   if (tcb->dspace != NULL)
132:     {
133:       /* Set the PIC base register (probably R10) to the address of the
134:        * alloacated D-Space region.
135:        */
136: 
137:       xcp->regs[REG_PIC] = (uint32_t)tcb->dspace->region;
138:     }
139: 
140: #ifdef CONFIG_NXFLAT
141:   /* Make certain that bit 0 is set in the main entry address.  This
142:    * is only an issue when NXFLAT is enabled.  NXFLAT doesn't know
143:    * anything about thumb; the addresses that NXFLAT sets are based
144:    * on file header info and won't have bit 0 set.
145:    */
146: 
147:   tcb->entry.main = (main_t)((uint32_t)tcb->entry.main | 1);
148: #endif
149: #endif /* CONFIG_PIC */
150: 
151:   /* All tasks start via a stub function in kernel space.  So all
152:    * tasks must start in privileged thread mode.  If CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED
153:    * is defined, then that stub function will switch to unprivileged
154:    * mode before transferring control to the user task.
155:    */
156: 
157:   xcp->regs[REG_EXC_RETURN] = EXC_RETURN_THREAD;
158: 
159:   xcp->regs[REG_CONTROL] = getcontrol() & ~CONTROL_NPRIV;
160: 
161: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_FPU
162:   xcp->regs[REG_FPSCR]  |= ARM_FPSCR_LTPSIZE_NONE;
163: #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_FPU */
164: 
165:   /* Enable or disable interrupts, based on user configuration */
166: 
167: #ifdef CONFIG_SUPPRESS_INTERRUPTS
168: 
169:   xcp->regs[REG_BASEPRI] = NVIC_SYSH_DISABLE_PRIORITY;
170: 
171: #else /* CONFIG_SUPPRESS_INTERRUPTS */
172: 
173:   xcp->regs[REG_BASEPRI] = 0;
174: 
175: #endif /* CONFIG_SUPPRESS_INTERRUPTS */
176: 
177: #if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT) && defined(CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV)
178:   xcp->nkernels = 1;
179: #endif

191: noinline_function void arm_initialize_stack(void)

194:   uint32_t stack = stacklim + INTSTACK_SIZE;
195:   uint32_t temp = 0;

197:   __asm__ __volatile__

201:       "bne 1f\n"
202: 
203:       /* Initialize PSP */
204: 
205:       "mrs %1, msp\n"
206:       "msr psp, %1\n"
207: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
208:       "mrs %1, msplim\n"
209:       "msr psplim, %1\n"
210: #else
211:       "mov %1, #0\n"
212:       "msr psplim, %1\n"
213: #endif
214:       "isb sy\n"
215: 
216:       /* Select PSP */
217: 
218:       "mrs %1, CONTROL\n"
